summary: Paul Ricœur (1913–2005) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Rennes and Paris, and held posts at Strasbourg, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Nanterre, Louvain, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bernhard Geiger at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1921). He held positions at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton University, and Yale University (1944–1966).

Paul Theodor Hoffmann (1891–1952) specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Berlin, Munich, Grenoble Alpes, and Tübingen, where he completed his Ph.D. under Richard von Garbe. In 1941, he directed Hamburg's Theaterwissenschaftliches Institut.

Paul Thieme (1905–2001) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Emil Sieg, Heinrich Lüders, Wilhelm Schulze, and Kamalakanta Mishra. His academic posts included Allahabad, Breslau, Halle, Frankfurt, Yale, and Tübingen.

Paul Tillich (1886–1965) was a theologian and philosopher who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle, and Breslau. He held faculty positions at Berlin, Marburg, Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary, Harvard, and the University of Chicago.

Paul W. Kroll (b. 1948) is a sinologist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan around 1969–1976. He served as Associate Professor and chair of Oriental Languages and Literatures at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1979.

Paul Whalley (1839–1920) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1857–1864). He served as a civil servant in the Bengal Civil Service (1860–1890) and Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs (1871–1872).

Paul Wilfred O'Brien (1908–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley around 1935–1941. He taught at the Pontifical College of St. Pius X from 1958 to 1965.

Paul Williams (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indian and Tibetan philosophy. He studied at Sussex and Oxford (DPhil) and was a fellow at Wadham College, visiting professor at Calgary, and professor at the University of Bristol (c. 1980–2011).
Paul Wodilla (1903–1982) was an Indology scholar who studied at Comenius University and received his Ph.D. from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg by 1928.

Paul de Lagarde (1827–1891) was a scholar of religion, linguistics, and Iranian-Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle under Friedrich Rückert and August Tholuck, later holding posts at the University of Halle and the University of Göttingen.

Paul-Émile Dumont (1879–1968) was an Indologist. He studied at Brussels, Bologna, and under Pullè, Oldenberg, Deussen, Macdonell, and Caland. He taught at Kiel and the Université libre de Bruxelles before becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Indology at Johns Hopkins.

Paula Arai is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees from Kalamazoo College and Harvard, studying under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Wilfred Cantwell Smith, and John Bunyan Spencer. She held posts at Vanderbilt, LSU, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Paulina Kolata is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who earned her Ph.D. at Manchester (2015–2019). She has held posts at Chester, Manchester, Copenhagen, and Harvard (2025).
Paulina Koniuch is a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who completed her bachelor's degree at the University of Warsaw (2017–2020) and became a faculty member there in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew (1748–1806) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, Sapienza, and San Pancrazio. He served at the Malabar Mission, Saint Joseph's Seminary, San Pancrazio, and the Pontifical Urban University.
Pavankumar Satuluri is an Indologist working in computational linguistics. He has held positions at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (attested 2024–2025).

Pavel Grintser (1928–2009) was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Peterson (1946–1951). He later held posts at the Gorky Institute of World Literature (1969–2009) and the Russian State University for the Humanities (1992–2009).

Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov (1814–1875) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Moscow and St. Petersburg under Aleksej Boldyrev, Robert Lenz, and Franz Bopp, and held professorships in Sanskrit and Oriental Languages at Kazan and Moscow State Universities.

Pavel Konstantinovich Portnyagin (1903–1977) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies scholar who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (1932) and worked as a translator at the Uzbek Karakul Sheep Breeding Research Institute.
